Original code passes test_format_signature; my changes cause failure. Need to understand why old code works despite type mismatch: ClassDocumenter.get_doc returns List[str], but DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature expects List[List[str]].

Trace for formatsig('class','F2',F2,None,None): ClassDocumenter.format_signature runs; doc_as_attr False (F2.__name__==objpath[-1]), calls super().format_signature() → DocstringSignatureMixin.format_signature. args None and autodoc_docstring_signature True, so _find_signature() called. self.get_doc() resolves to ClassDocumenter.get_doc (self is ClassDocumenter instance; its get_doc takes priority in MRO: ClassDocumenter → DocstringSignatureMixin → ModuleLevelDocumenter → Documenter). DocstringSignatureMixin.get_doc checks _new_docstrings then super().get_doc(), but never reached via self.

Because first docstring's first char doesn't match signature regex, _find_signature returns None; `if result is not None` fails; falls through to super().format_signature() in DocstringSignatureMixin → ModuleLevelDocumenter → Documenter.format_signature. There self.args still None, so introspects via _call_format_args. For class this may call class signature, not __init__; yet test expects (a1, a2, kw1=True, kw2=False). Need to inspect Documenter.format_signature (it calls format_args when args is None; ClassDocumenter.format_args uses _get_signature for introspection) to see how docstring-based signature is actually obtained.
